Angie Nixon

Democratic candidate for United States Senator, Florida · Challenger

Florida state representative (House District 13); bookstore owner; former community and union organizer

Angie Nixon is a Jacksonville Democrat who has been in the Florida House of Representatives since 2020. She won the Democratic nomination for U.S. Senate in the August 18, 2026 primary, defeating Alex Vindman. In the November 3, 2026 special election she faces Republican U.S. Sen. Ashley Moody, who holds the seat by appointment.

Where Nixon stands

Health care
Supports Medicare for All and favors moving to it in steps. Says people should not go bankrupt because they go to the doctor.
Housing
Supports rent stabilization, including a national rent stabilization standard, to address housing costs.
Minimum wage
Supports raising the federal minimum wage. Says she helped lead the coalition work behind Florida's $15-an-hour minimum wage increase.
Taxes
Her platform calls for a 5% annual wealth tax on billionaires.
Immigration
Her platform calls for abolishing ICE. Says she would work to stop the Trump administration's deportation and detention policies.
Policing
Says she supports continued police funding and rejects the claim that she wants to defund the police.
Ethics and government accountability
Says Sen. Moody gained from stock trading while on health committees. Calls for a Justice Department investigation of the Hope Florida funds; Moody denies wrongdoing.
Foreign policy / Cuba
Says she is open to lifting the U.S. trade embargo on Cuba. Supports shifting foreign policy toward diplomacy.
Technology / Section 230
Argues online platforms should lose their federal liability protections and that social media executives should be held legally accountable for disinformation.
Education
Says she supports fully funded public schools.

Background

  • Member, Florida House of Representatives, 2020–present (District 14, 2020–2022; District 13, 2022–present)
  • Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Florida, 2026 (won Aug. 18, 2026 primary)
  • Bookstore owner; former community and union organizer; background in higher education
  • Education: B.A., University of Florida
  • Born February 27, 1984, in Jacksonville, Florida
  • Member of the Working Families Party; joined Democratic Socialists of America in June 2026
